title: Time and causality in quantum gravity
abstract: The problem of time in quantum gravity is often presented as a consequence of applying quantum theory to general relativity. These notes adopt a broader perspective. We first examine how time enters classical mechanics, relativity, quantum theory, and quantum field theory, distinguishing three principal aspects: causal order, temporal duration, and the present. This analysis shows that the conceptual difficulties associated with time do not arise only when gravity is quantised. Tensions between causal structure, clocks, observables, and measurement are already present in the theories from which quantum gravity is constructed. We then survey responses to the problem of time across the principal approaches to quantum gravity. These include canonical and Wheeler-DeWitt quantisation, path-integral and histories formulations, perturbative and background-dependent approaches, causal sets, and twistor theory. The programmes are compared according to whether they retain an external time, render time problematic through quantisation, or incorporate causal or temporal structure into their foundations. Particular emphasis is placed on questions arising from quantum foundations and relativistic quantum information. We conclude by examining linearised gravity and weak-gravity quantum systems. This regime shows that the problem of time is not confined to Planck-scale physics, but arises already in attempts to provide a predictive and operationally meaningful quantum description of spacetime near flat geometry.
summary: This paper provides a broad conceptual analysis of the problem of time in quantum gravity, arguing that the difficulties are inherent in the structure of time itself, not just at the Planck scale. It distinguishes between causal order, temporal duration, and the 'present' by surveying major theoretical approaches like causal sets and canonical quantization. The work is crucial for understanding the foundational assumptions required for a consistent quantum theory of spacetime.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental 'problem of time' that arises when attempting to reconcile quantum mechanics with general relativity, arguing that conceptual difficulties exist even before quantizing gravity.
main_result: The problem of time is not confined to Planck-scale physics, as conceptual tensions between causal structure, temporal duration, and measurement are present in theories describing weak-gravity regimes.
method: The analysis adopts a broad conceptual framework, distinguishing between three aspects of time (causal order, temporal duration, and the present) and surveying various quantum gravity approaches.
model_or_system: The scope covers classical mechanics, special/general relativity, quantum field theory, and various quantum gravity formalisms including canonical quantization (Wheeler-DeWitt), path integrals, causal sets, and twistor theory.
key_observables: Causal order ($\alpha \prec  eta$), temporal duration (measure), and the structure of observables related to measurement.
important_parameters: Planck scale, weak-gravity limit, and the distinction between metric and causal structures.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the conceptual difficulties stem from conflating distinct mathematical and physical notions of time.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the three aspects of time across classical and quantum theories, then surveys and compares major quantum gravity approaches (canonical, path-integral, causal sets, etc.) based on how they treat time, concluding with an examination of the weak-gravity limit.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity, the deep dive into the structure of time (order vs. measure) and the role of causality is foundational for any theory involving time evolution, connecting to quantum foundations.
